facebook.content_angle: Six-beat kick efficiency — how most freestyle swimmers default to a two-beat kick and leave measurable speed on the table without realising it
facebook.post_text:
Most swimmers are leaving 10% freestyle speed on the table. 🔥

You're pulling hard, rotating well, breathing clean — but your kick is working against you.

A two-beat kick keeps you balanced. It does not drive you forward.

👉 Elite freestyle sprinters use a six-beat kick — six leg strikes per stroke cycle
👉 The continuous propulsion from a six-beat pattern reduces drag and stabilises hip rotation simultaneously
👉 Swimmers who shift from two-beat to six-beat record an average 10.21% improvement in 50m split times within four weeks of targeted drill work

The kick isn't just a float. It's an engine. ⚡

✔️ Drill it in isolation first — kick sets without a board, arms at your sides, feel the tempo
✔️ Then integrate: match kick tempo to your stroke rate in 25m efforts
✔️ Time your 50m before and after four weeks — the data will do the convincing

Are you training your kick as hard as your pull?
